learning_outcomes.description: Evaluate limits, derivatives, and integrals, explain the underlying mathematical basis, interpret the results geometrically, and perform calculations associated with a number of applications;
Understand and evaluate the limits of sequences and series, and use them to approximate functions;
Work with matrices and vectors including a complete understanding of the behaviour of an m * n linear system;
Understand the concept of invertibility for matrices, know many criteria for invertibility and be able to find inverses;
Understand abstract concepts in linear algebra such as vector space, dimension and basis, and be able to construct simple proofs involving these concepts;

assessments.task_description:
Ten problems will be released in Week 3. Students are encouraged to work through these problems over the following weeks, using them to develop their mathematical understanding and problem-solving skills.

In Week 7, students will complete a 60-minute quiz consisting of three questions randomly selected from the ten previously released problems.

Students will be expected to demonstrate their ability to solve these problems independently under supervised assessment conditions.

assessments.task_description:
Part A of the end of semester examination assesses students' competency in fundamental mathematical skills and concepts. It consists of 20 questions, each marked as either correct or incorrect, with no partial marks awarded.

Part A contributes 15% towards the final course grade, awarded on a pass/fail basis:

Part B of the end of semester exam contributes 40% towards the final course grade

Part B contains a range of short-answer and problem-solving questions designed to assess students' mathematical understanding and ability to apply course concepts and techniques. Partial marks may be awarded for appropriate mathematical working, even where the final answer is incorrect.

Calculators are not allowed.

The End of Semester Examination will be an in-person, paper-based exam for all students.

Internally enrolled students

The end-of-semester exam will be an in-person, paper-based exam. Students will sit the exam at the St Lucia Campus.

Externally enrolled students

The end-of-semester exam will be an in-person, paper-based exam. UQ Examinations will contact students directly to confirm arrangements. You will either sit the exam at the St Lucia campus (if you live within 200km radius of the campus) or will be directed to nominate an exam centre by a certain date. 

Please ensure you update your semester address in Si-net at the start of the semester.

One reminder will be sent and students who fail to nominate an exam centre will be automatically assigned to the St Lucia campus. Late nominations will not be accepted.

learning_activities.topic:
Lecture

Students may choose to attend either Zoom live lectures or view the online UQ Extend lectures. Lectures are centered around the workbook, so it is vital that students have their workbook with them for both the live lectures and the online UQ Extend lectures. As well as completing the workbook in a comprehensive manner, students will be provided with additional material and examples. Students electing to simply download the completed workbook from Blackboard after each chapter is finished will hence be missing material.
